read_prompt: Read the image file {path}. It is an enlarged crop of a few printed lines from one column of an 1854 Hebrew-English lexicon (Gesenius, Robinson translation). Transcribe every complete printed text line exactly, one array element per printed line, top to bottom. Preserve spelling, capitalisation, punctuation, printed abbreviations, section marks and end-of-line hyphenation. Hebrew, Aramaic, Arabic, Syriac, Greek and Ethiopic must be Unicode text with every visible vowel point, dagesh, shin or sin dot, accent and diacritic, and with no point that is not printed; write them in logical order with no bidi control characters, keep the words of a right-to-left phrase in the order they are read, and keep the printed left-to-right order of separate items in a list. Transcribe the letters actually printed even when they are not the dictionary spelling: never insert or drop a vav or yod, and never replace a form with a more familiar one. Distinguish Arabic from Syriac by the letter shapes. If a line is only partially visible at the top or bottom edge, omit it entirely rather than guessing. Never add, reorder, translate, normalise or omit anything that is fully visible. If the crop contains no text, return an empty array.

lines.text: lages around that city, elsewhere בְּנוֹת
הָעִיר; as עָרֵי חֶשְׁבּוֹן Josh. 13, 17. Jer. 34, 1.
But עָרֵי עֲרוֹעֵר Is. 17, 2, see in עֲרוֹעֵר no. 1.
—Proverbially Ecc. 10, 15 the labour of
the foolish wearieth him, because he
knoweth not לָלֶכֶת אֶל־עִיר to go to the city,
i. e. cannot find his way to the city; the
figure being taken from an awkward
rustic who loses his way on the most
beaten road; comp. Germ. ‘ er weiss sich
nicht zu finden.’ In Ps. 73, 20 בָּעִיר is
for בְּהָעִיר inf. Hiph. of r. עוּר I.—Spec.
עִיר is also put:
a) For a part of a larger city, espec.
as fortified by a separate wall; like Gr.
πόλις see Passow, Engl. Old city, New
city. So עִיר דָּוִד the city of David, i. e.
the citadel on Zion, a part of Jerusalem,
ἡ ἄνω πόλις, 2 Sam. 5, 7. 9. 6, 10. 12.
[Later the name city of David seems to
have sometimes included the whole of
Jerusalem; see Biblioth. Sacr. 1843, p.
הַתִּיכוֹנָה the middle city, the middle part
of Jerusalem, 2 K. 20. 4 Cheth. where

lines.reread: of Jerusalem, 2 K. 20. 4 Cheth. where
lines.note: The mark after "20" is a round dot sitting on the baseline with no descending tail — a period, not a comma — so Reading B is correct (even though a comma would be the lexicon's usual chapter/verse convention).

lines.text: Keri has חָצֵר. So עִיר הַמַּיִם the water-
city, part of the city Rabbah, 2 Sam. 12,
27; עִיר בֵּית הַבַּעַל the city of the house
of Baal, a part of Samaria so called
from the temple of Baal, prob. the enclo-
sure of the temple, τέμενος. 2 K. 10, 25.
b) As in Engl. the city for its inhabi-
tants, the people of a city; 1 Sam. 4, 13
וַתִּזְעַק כָּל־הָעִיר all the city cried out. Is.
14, 31. Here too belongs the phrase
עִיר מְתִים the city of men, i. e. the multi-
tude, crowd of men, Deut. 2, 34. 3, 6.
where read מְתִם for מְתֹם. See Thesaur.

lines.note: Under the first word the mem carries a vertical two-dot sheva (not a horizontal tsere) and the middle letter has a single dot (hiriq) beneath it; the middle letter in both words is tav with a left foot, not he/heth. Second word has holem over tav. Matches Reading A and the article's context (מְתִים, Judg. 20:48 מְתֹם, cross-ref to עִיר II. b).

lines.text: p. 830, and עִיר II. b.
c) With genit. of a people or country,
the chief city, metropolis; as עִיר יְהוּדָה
the city of Judah, i. e. Jerusalem, 2 Chr.
Proper names of cities are: aa) עִיר
הַמֶּלַח the City of Salt in the desert of
Judah, near the Dead Sea, Josh. 15, 62.
bb) עִיר נָחָשׁ (city of serpents) Ir-na-
hash, the site of which is unknown, 1
cc) עִיר שֶׁמֶשׁ (city of the sun) Ir-she-
mesh, in the territory of Dan, Josh. 19,
51. Prob. the same with Beth-shemesh;
see Bibl. Res. in Palest. III. p. 19.
dd) עִיר הַתְּמָרִים the City of palm-trees,
i. q. יְרִיחוֹ Jericho, so called from the
multitude of palm-trees growing there,
see Plin. H. N. 5. 14. Tacit. Hist. 5. 6.
ee) For עִיר הַהֶרֶס see under הֶרֶס.
2. Ir, pr. n. of a man 1 Chr. 7, 12; for
which in v. 7 עִירִי.

will not come in wrath. b) Of mind,
